content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.67 or +1.00) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (especially -0.00 or 0.00) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp spikes, then undercorrects after drops — adjust for lagged momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is bullish (last 3–5 days +ve), but fails to account for short-term volatility.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overestimates mid-term price stability — ignore sentiment-driven momentum in such cases.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs as “sustained” — sentiment shifts often trigger sharp corrections within 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for reversal risk.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment history when price is trending sideways — force sentiment weighting into forecast adjustments.
